notes: Structured query templates for the Content Decay Detector, migrated from the legacy generate_query/get_data_insights flow to the current TMR MCP. Two connectors: gsc (site URL account IDs) and ga4 (numeric property IDs). Field IDs are raw. Dates NOT stored — runtime resolves the chosen comparison window (30/60/90 days, default 30) AND its immediately-preceding equal-length window; each query runs for BOTH so step 7 can compute period-over-period decay. No currency. ORGANIC-ONLY handling for the GA4 query: session_default_channel_grouping is included as a dimension so synthesis keeps only 'Organic Search' rows (avoids guessing connector-side filter syntax). Both queries validated clean against live gsc + ga4 accounts. GSC data lags ~2-3 days.

queries.title: GA4 Organic Session & Engagement Decay
queries.organic_filter: Keep only rows where session_default_channel_grouping == 'Organic Search' during synthesis, then aggregate per landing_page.

decay_logic_reference.candidate_threshold: Flag if clicks_drop > 20% OR organic_sessions_drop > 20%; exclude if combined clicks in either period < 50
decay_logic_reference.severity: Critical >=60 or any metric >60% drop; High 40-59 or 40-60% drop; Medium 20-39 or 20-40% drop
decay_logic_reference.root_cause_cases: A Visibility Loss (impressions & clicks both down >15%); B SERP Issue (impressions stable, CTR down >15%); C Tracking Mismatch (GSC clicks stable, GA4 sessions down >20% - flag); D Engagement Decay (sessions stable, engaged sessions or key events down >25%); E Mixed/Unclear
